2:3.headline: שופט, "judge", here means the king
2:3.body: Ibn Ezra says שופט means the king, and the proof is that "all her princes" die with him. Malbim says he is the chief judge, which is their king.

sources.quote: שופט הוא מלך והעד וכל שריה אהרוג עמו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says שופט is a king, and the witness is "and all her princes I will kill with him".

sources.quote: שופט, הוא השופט הכללי שהוא המלך שלהם
sources.says: Malbim says the שופט is the general judge, who is their king.

sources.quote: עם מלך מואב
sources.says: Radak says "with him" means with the king of Moab.

2:6.headline: The "righteous" they sell is the one who is right in court
2:6.body: Radak says צדיק here means a person who is in the right in his case, not a saint. Rashi says the judges sold him by ruling against him for a bribe.

sources.quote: ופירוש צדיק שהוא צדיק בדינו
sources.says: Radak says צדיק means one who is righteous in his case.

sources.quote: הַדַּיָּנִין הָיוּ מוֹכְרִים אֶת מִי שֶׁהָיָה זַכַּאי בַּדִּין בְּכֶסֶף שֹׁחַד
sources.says: Rashi says the judges sold the man who was innocent in the case for bribe money.

sources.quote: על השופטים ידבר והעד צדיק בריבו בהשפטו והנו נחשב כאילו מכרוהו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it speaks of judges, and the man is in the right in his dispute but is treated as though sold.

2:6.headline: A pair of sandals, a lock on a field, or a sale?
2:6.body: Metzudat David reads נעלים as shoes, the tiny bribe the judge took. Rashi reads it from נעילה, locking: they forced the poor man to sell so they could fence in their fields. Radak adds that a sandal was the sign that closes a sale.

sources.quote: מטין דין האביון בעבור מחיר שוחד מנעלים לרגליהם
sources.says: Metzudat David says they bend the poor man's case for the price of a bribe of shoes for their feet.

sources.quote: וְזֶה עוֹקֵף עָלָיו וְנוֹטְלָהּ בְּדָמִים קַלִּים כְּדֵי לִגְדּוֹר וְלִנְעוֹל כָּל שְׂדוֹתָיו יַחַד
sources.says: Rashi says one buys the field cheaply in order to fence and lock all his fields together.

sources.quote: מחייבין את הזכאי כדי שיצטרך העני למכור שדהו בקנין גמור שהוא בנעל שנאמר שלף איש נעלו
sources.says: Radak says they rule against the innocent so the poor man must sell his field in a complete sale, done with a sandal, as in "a man drew off his sandal".

2:7.headline: Who is "the girl" the father and son go to?
2:7.body: Rashi says she is a betrothed girl. Radak says she is a woman the father has already had. Ibn Ezra says she is one known girl, shared by father and son without shame.

sources.quote: אֶל הַנַּעֲרָה. הַמְאוֹרָסָה
sources.says: Rashi says the girl is the betrothed one.

sources.quote: ולא יבוש הבן מאביו לבעול בעולת אביו
sources.says: Radak says the son is not ashamed before his father to lie with his father's woman.

sources.quote: עד שלא יבוש ללכת איש עם אביו עם נערה ידוע
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a man is not ashamed to go with his father to a known girl.

2:8.headline: יטו means "bend" in verse 7, but "recline at a meal" here
2:8.body: The same verb was about bending the poor man's way. Here Rashi says it means reclining at a meal, since a diner leans on his left side. Radak says a reclining person tilts himself.

sources.quote: יַטּוּ. לְשׁוֹן מְסִבָּה, שֶׁכָּל מְסִבַּת סְעוּדָה בַּהֲטָיָה הִיא, שֶׁהוּא נִסְמָךְ עַל שְׂמֹאלוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means reclining, since every banquet is done reclining, leaning on the left.

sources.quote: וההסיבה נקראת הטייה לפי שמטה אדם עצמו כשוכב
sources.says: Radak says reclining is called הטייה because a person tilts himself as he lies down.

sources.quote: מענין הסבה, ונמצא הרבה בלשון המשנה
sources.says: Malbim says it is from the idea of reclining, and is found often in the language of the Mishnah.

2:8.headline: "Wine of the fined": wine bought with fines
2:8.body: Rashi, Radak and Metzudat Zion all read ענושים as fined in money. The judges fined people, then spent the money on wine to drink in the house of their gods.

sources.quote: שֶׁעוֹנְשִׁים אוֹתָם מָמוֹן וְשׁוֹתִים בּוֹ יַיִן
sources.says: Rashi says they fine them money and drink wine with it.

sources.quote: מל׳ עונש ממון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from the word for a money penalty.

sources.quote: שהם עונשים אותם כסף וזהב וישתו בו בית אלהיהם
sources.says: Radak says they fine them silver and gold and drink with it in the house of their god.

2:9.headline: Tall as cedars: exact height, or the language of exaggeration?
2:9.body: Maimonides lists this verse among the prophets' exaggerations, said loosely and not exactly. Malbim reads the height as the Amorites' rule and power, and Radak uses it to show they were the strongest of the seven nations.

sources.quote: ובהתאם לכך נאמר: "[וְאָנֹכִי הִשְׁמַדְתִּי אֶת הָאֱמֹרִי מִפְּנֵיהֶם] אֲשֶׁר כְּגֹבַהּ אֲרָזִים גָּבְהוֹ [וְחָסֹן הוּא כָּאַלּוֹנִים]" (עמוס ב,ט). אופן זה מצוי לרוב בדברי הנביאים כולם, כוונתי לדברים הנאמרים באופן של הגזמה והפרזה
sources.says: Maimonides cites this verse as an example of the prophets' exaggeration, not a precise statement.

sources.quote: כי היה כגובה ארזים גבהו במלוכה ושלטנות, וחסון הוא כאלונים מצד הכח והגבורה
sources.says: Malbim says the height was in kingship and rule, and the oak-like strength was in power and might.

sources.quote: וזכר האמרי כי הוא החזק שבשבע האומות כמו שאמר אשר כגובה ארזים גבהו
sources.says: Radak says the Amorite is named because he was the strongest of the seven nations, as the verse says "tall as cedars".

2:9.headline: חסן means strong, and gives the name חסין for God
2:9.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion say חסן means strength, as in Isaiah 1:31. Maimonides says the divine name חסין in Psalm 89:9 comes from this strength, and cites this verse.

sources.quote: וכן השם "חֲסִין" (תהילים פט,ט) נגזר מכוח: "וְחָסֹן הוּא כָּאַלּוֹנִים"
sources.says: Maimonides says the name חסין is derived from strength, as in "and he is strong like the oaks".

sources.quote: ענין חוזק כמו והיה החסון לנעורת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means strength, as in "the strong one shall be tow".

sources.quote: תקיף כמו והיה החסון לנעורת
sources.says: Radak says it means powerful, as in "the strong one shall be tow".

2:11.headline: Nazirites, or teachers set apart?
2:11.body: Rashi follows Targum Jonathan: these are teachers who kept apart from common ways and studied Torah, and נזירה always means setting apart. In verse 12 he says they were given wine so they could not teach, since a drunk may not teach. Metzudat Zion reads it as one who keeps from wine.

sources.quote: תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: לְמַלְפִין, שֶׁהָיוּ פְרוּשִׁין מִדַּרְכֵי עַם הָאָרֶץ וְעוֹסְקִים בַּתּוֹרָה. אֵין נְזִירָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן פְּרִישָׁה
sources.says: Rashi says Targum Jonathan renders it "teachers", people kept apart from common ways who study Torah, since נזירה always means separation.

sources.quote: וּמֵעוּלֵימֵיכוֹן לְמַלְפִין
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders "from your young men, nazirites" as "from your young men, teachers".

sources.quote: שֶׁלֹּא יוֹרוּ אֶתְכֶם, שֶׁהַשִּׁכּוֹר אָסוּר לְהוֹרוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says they made them drink so they could not teach, because a drunk is forbidden to teach.

sources.quote: הוא ענין פרישה כי פורש עצמו מן היין והטומאה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means separation, because he keeps himself from wine and impurity.

2:11.headline: "Is this not so?" or "is even this missing?"
2:11.body: Rashi and Ibn Ezra read האף אין זאת as a challenge: can you deny it? Malbim reads it as a charge: have you cancelled even these safeguards, so that no prophets or nazirites remain among you?

sources.quote: בִּתְמִיהָּה, כְּלוֹמַר כְּלוּם אַתֶּם יְכוֹלִים לְהַכְחִישׁ אֶת זֹאת
sources.says: Rashi says it is asked in wonder: can you deny this?

sources.quote: תוכלו לכחש כי לא עשיתי זאת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says: can you deny that I did this?

sources.quote: האף ההכנות שישמרו אתכם מחטאים אלה תבטלו? עד שגם זאת אין ביניכם לא נביאים ולא נזירים
sources.says: Malbim says: will you even cancel the safeguards against these sins, until there are no prophets or nazirites among you?

2:16.headline: "Naked" he flees: without clothes, or without weapons?
2:16.body: Rashi translates ערום as stripped, and says it means without weapons. Radak and Ibn Ezra say he takes off his clothes, because they are too heavy to run in.

sources.quote: עַרְטִילַאי בְּלֹא כְּלִי זַיִן
sources.says: Rashi says ערום means stripped, without weapons.

sources.quote: וטעם ערום שיפשוט בגדיו שלא יכבדו עליו וינוס קל מהרה
sources.says: Radak says ערום means he strips off his clothes so they are not heavy on him, and flees light and fast.

sources.quote: שיכבדו עליו בגדיו בברחו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says his clothes would be heavy on him as he flees.

3:2.headline: 'Only you have I known': here knowing means loving
3:2.body: God knows every nation, so 'only you have I known' cannot mean plain knowing. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as 'only you have I loved', which is why Israel is held to account.

sources.quote: רַק אֶתְכֶם יָדַעְתִּי. אָהַבְתִּי
sources.says: Rashi says 'I knew' means 'I loved'.

sources.quote: ידעתי. ענין אהבה וכן מה אדם ותדעהו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means love, as in 'what is man that You know him' in Psalms.

sources.quote: ידעתי, בא לפעמים אצל ה' להורות על ההשגחה היתירה
sources.says: Malbim says that when said of God, 'knowing' can mean special, close care.

3:4.headline: Young lion by its den, grown lion out in the forest
3:4.body: The verse uses two words for lion. Malbim says the grown אריה hunts in the forest, while the young כפיר stays by its den, so each is placed where it belongs.

sources.quote: האריה הוא הגדול והכפיר הוא הקטן וכבר הובא (הושע ה' י"ד) שהכפיר לא יצא חוץ למקומו לטרוף, לז"א במעונתו, והאריה יוצא על טרפו עז"א ביער
sources.says: Malbim says the כפיר is the young lion, which does not leave its den to hunt, while the grown lion goes out into the forest.

sources.quote: כפיר. ארי בחור
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says a כפיר is a young lion.

3:7.headline: What makes a prophet: the one told God's secret
3:7.body: Some linked the word נביא to speech. Ibn Ezra rejects that and uses this verse instead: a prophet is the one to whom God tells His secret.

sources.quote: רק פירושו הוא נביא שאגלה לו סודי כדרך כי אם גלה סודו אל עבדיו הנביאים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra rejects deriving נביא from ניב, speech, and says a prophet is one to whom God reveals His secret, citing this verse.

sources.quote: וטעם סודו כי לא נודע הדבר עד שיודיעהו האל יתברך ע"י עבדיו הנביאים
sources.says: Radak says it is called God's 'secret' because no one knows it until He tells His prophets.

3:8.headline: A prophet who hears God cannot stay silent
3:8.body: 'Who would not prophesy?' Maimonides reads it as a fact about prophets: the call presses on them and gives them no rest, like Jeremiah, who tried to stop and could not.

sources.quote: וזאת היא משמעות דברי הנביא האחר: "ה' אֱלֹהִים דִּבֶּר, מִי לֹא יִנָּבֵא"
sources.says: Maimonides says the flow of prophecy drives prophets to speak and gives them no rest, even when it harms them, and reads this verse that way.

sources.quote: ואיך יוכל לעמוד שלא ימלא את דברי אשר צויתיו
sources.says: Radak says that as a lion's roar frightens everyone, a prophet who hears God cannot hold back from delivering His words.

3:12.headline: A scrap of ear: the bit of the sheep a lion leaves
3:12.body: בדל אזן is the hard cartilage of the ear. Metzudat Zion says the word has no parallel, and Radak says the lion leaves it because there is no meat on it.

sources.quote: בְּדַל אֹזֶן. חַסְחוּס דְּאוּדָן
sources.says: Rashi, using the Aramaic, says it is the cartilage of the ear.

sources.quote: בדל אזן. ת״י חסחוס והוא הקשה שבאזן ואין לו דמיון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the hard part of the ear, and the word has no parallel.

sources.quote: וזכר בדל אזן והוא הקשה שבאזן כתרגומו חסחוס דאודן לפי שאין בו בשר ויניחנו האריה
sources.says: Radak says the lion leaves the ear's cartilage because it has no meat on it.

4:1.headline: 'Cows of Bashan' are not cows: who does the Targum say?
4:1.body: Rashi, Radak and Ibn Ezra say the 'cows' are the wives of the nobles, fat and pampered like cattle in rich pasture. The Targum has 'the wealthy' instead.

sources.quote: נְשֵׁי הַשָּׂרִים וְהַסְּגָנִים, וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: עֲתִּירֵי נִכְסַיָּא
sources.says: Rashi says they are the wives of the nobles and officials, and that Jonathan translated 'the owners of wealth'.

sources.quote: ודמה נשי המלכים והשרים הגדולים לפרות הבשן לפי שהן בעלות תענוג והן שמנות ויפות
sources.says: Radak says he likened the wives of the kings and great nobles to the cows of Bashan because they live in luxury and are fat and fine.

sources.quote: עַתִּירֵי נִכְסַיָא דִבְטוּרָא דְשֹׁמְרוֹן
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'the wealthy of the mountain of Samaria'.

4:1.headline: They 'oppress' the poor only by telling their husbands to bring wine
4:1.body: The women do not rob anyone themselves. Ibn Ezra asks how they can be called oppressors, and the answer is that their demands push their husbands to take from the poor.

sources.quote: איך הם עשקות באומרים לבעליהם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra explains how they are oppressors: by what they say to their husbands.

sources.quote: וחוזר ומפרש שאינם עושקות בידיהן רק הן האומרות לבעליהן הביאה יין ונשתה
sources.says: Metzudat David says they do not oppress with their own hands, but are the ones who tell their husbands to bring wine.

sources.quote: הוצרכו בעליהן לעשוק ולחמוס לתת להן יין לסבוא
sources.says: Malbim says their husbands had to rob and plunder to give them wine to drink.

4:2.headline: Sworn 'by His holiness', or by heaven?
4:2.body: Ibn Ezra and Radak read בקדשו as heaven, like 'I lift my hand to heaven'. Metzudat David glosses it as 'by His holiness'.

sources.quote: בקדשו - בשמים, כמו: כי אשא אל שמים ידי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says בקדשו means 'by heaven', like 'I lift my hand to heaven'.

sources.quote: בקדשו. הוא השמים
sources.says: Radak says בקדשו is the heavens.

sources.quote: בקדשו. בקדושתו
sources.says: Metzudat David glosses בקדשו as 'by His holiness'.

4:3.headline: Gaps in the wall, or loose women?
4:3.body: Rashi reads ופרצים as the gaps in the wall that the women flee through. Malbim reads it as פריצות: immoral women who come out to meet them.

sources.quote: וּבְפִרְצֵי הַחוֹמָה תֵּצֶאנָה שָׁם לָנוּס
sources.says: Rashi says they will go out through the breaches of the wall to flee.

sources.quote: תצא אשה זונה פרוצה בפריצות לקבל אותה
sources.says: Malbim says an immoral woman will come out to receive her.

sources.quote: שיצאו לקראתה פריצים, כמו והוליד בן פריץ, נשים פרוצות
sources.says: Malbim says the word can mean the immoral who come out toward her, loose women.

4:3.headline: Palace, women's quarters, a mountain, or 'your pride'?
4:3.body: Rashi reads it as 'you will throw off your pride', from an Aramaic word for the king's command, and the Targum has the mountains of Harmini. Others read it as a palace (Radak), a women's quarter (Malbim) or a place name (Ibn Ezra).

sources.quote: הַרְמָנָא דְמַלְכָּא הוּא צִוּוּי הַמֶּלֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi says the Aramaic word is 'the king's command'.

sources.quote: וְיִגְלוֹן יַתְכוֹן לְהַלְּאָה מִן טוּרֵי חַרְמִינֵי
sources.says: Rashi gives the Targum: they will exile you beyond the mountains of Harmini.

sources.quote: כי תשלכנה ארמון המלך שבצד החומה
sources.says: Radak gives his father's reading: you will be thrown to the king's palace beside the wall.

sources.quote: ושם הרמון מיוחד בלשונות המזרחיות על מקום המיוחד לנשים ופלגשים
sources.says: Malbim says הרמון is a word in eastern languages for the place set apart for women and concubines.

sources.quote: אולי ההרמונה שם מקום אחרי חומת שומרון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says perhaps it is the name of a place behind the wall of Samaria.

4:4.headline: 'Three days' or three years? When the tithes came
4:4.body: Metzudat Zion and Radak say ימים can mean years, as in 'ימים תהיה גאלתו', so the tithe came every third year. The Targum reads it as three days.

sources.quote: ימים. ענינו שנים כמו ימים תהיה גאולתו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ימים here means years, like 'its redemption shall be ימים'.

sources.quote: כמו ימים תהיה גאלתו כמו שאמר בתורה מקצה שלש שנים
sources.says: Radak says ימים means a year, as the Torah says 'at the end of three years'.

sources.quote: לִתְלָתָא יוֹמִין מַעֲסַרְתְּכוֹן
sources.says: The Targum reads it as 'for three days, your tithes'.

4:4.headline: 'In the morning': every morning, or left overnight?
4:4.body: Radak says לבקר means every single morning. He and Rashi also give a reading where the offerings are kept overnight until morning, against the Torah.

sources.quote: ופירוש לבקר כל בקר ובקר כלומר יום יום תביאו שם זבחיכם
sources.says: Radak says לבקר means every morning, that is, you bring your sacrifices there day by day.

sources.quote: והם מביאים לבקר זבחיהם כלומר מלינים אותם
sources.says: Radak says they bring their sacrifices 'to the morning', meaning they keep them overnight.

sources.quote: הַתּוֹרָה אָמְרָה ״לֹא יָלִין לַבֹּקֶר״
sources.says: Rashi says the Torah said 'it shall not stay overnight until morning', while for idolatry they bring it to the morning.

4:5.headline: Burn 'leavened' thank-offering, or what was taken by force?
4:5.body: חמץ is leaven, which the Torah does not allow on the altar, as Metzudat David and Malbim read it. The Targum, with Rashi and Radak, reads it like חמוץ in Isaiah 1:17: 'from what was seized by force'.

sources.quote: מִן אוֹנֶס, כְּמוֹ ״אַשְּׁרוּ חָמוֹץ״
sources.says: Rashi says Jonathan translated it 'from force', like 'set right the oppressed'.

sources.quote: ויונתן תירגם חמץ מן אשרו חמוץ
sources.says: Radak says Jonathan translated חמץ from 'אשרו חמוץ'.

sources.quote: אבל התורה לא צותה להקטיר מלחמי התודה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the Torah did not command burning any of the thank-offering breads.

sources.quote: שיקטרו תודה מחמץ כמו שבבית ה' הקריבו את התודה על חלות לחם חמץ
sources.says: Malbim says they proclaim to burn the thank-offering from leaven, as in the Temple they brought it on leavened loaves.

4:7.headline: The plot that got rain: a blessing, or also a curse?
4:7.body: Radak says תמטר is passive, 'be rained on', and תמטיר active, 'cause rain'. Rashi quotes the Talmud: both plots were a curse, since the rained-on one rots and the dry one withers.

sources.quote: אָמַר מַר: שְׁתֵּיהֶן לִקְלָלָה, זוֹ תֵּרָקֵב וְזוֹ תִּיבַשׁ
sources.says: Rashi quotes the Talmud: both are for a curse, this one rots and that one dries.

sources.quote: תמטר. מבנין נפעל
sources.says: Radak says תמטר is in the passive form.

sources.quote: תמטיר. מבנין הפעיל, ופירושו אשר לא תמטיר העב עליה
sources.says: Radak says תמטיר is in the causative form, meaning the cloud will not rain on it.

4:9.headline: 'Increasing your gardens': busy planting, or a bigger harvest?
4:9.body: Rashi and Radak read הרבות as 'to multiply': you busied yourselves planting more gardens. Metzudat David reads it as the abundance of your gardens' fruit.

sources.quote: שֶׁאַתֶּם עוֹסְקִים לְהַרְבּוֹת גַּנּוֹתֵיכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says you are busy multiplying your gardens.

sources.quote: מה יועיל לכם שתרבו לטעות גנות כרמים ותאינים וזתים
sources.says: Radak says what use is it that you plant many gardens of vines, figs and olives.

sources.quote: מרבית פרי גנותיכם
sources.says: Metzudat David glosses it as the abundance of the fruit of your gardens.

4:10.headline: בדרך מצרים: like the desert plague, or on the road to Egypt?
4:10.body: Rashi reads it as 'in the way I sent a plague on you in the desert after leaving Egypt'. Radak and Malbim read it as the road to Egypt, where Israel went to buy grain.

sources.quote: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁשָּׁלַחְתִּי עֲלֵיכֶם בַּמִּדְבָּר בְּצֵאתְכֶם מִמִּצְרַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says it is like the way I sent a plague on you in the desert when you left Egypt.

sources.quote: שהיו הולכים שם מפני הרעב להביא משם תבואה
sources.says: Radak says they were going there because of the famine, to bring grain from there.

sources.quote: ששלח בהם דבר בעת שהלכו בדרך מצרים
sources.says: Malbim says God sent a plague among them while they were going on the road to Egypt.

4:10.headline: Were the horses killed, or taken captive?
4:10.body: Rashi says the horses were killed along with the young men. Ibn Ezra and Radak read שבי as captive: the horses were taken.

sources.quote: שֶׁיֵּהָרְגוּ גַּם הַסּוּסִים
sources.says: Rashi says the horses will be killed too.

sources.quote: הרגתי בחוריכם ונשבו סוסיכם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says I killed your young men and your horses were taken captive.

sources.quote: והיו שובים הסוסים
sources.says: Radak says they were taking the horses captive.

sources.quote: עם שבי. כמו ושבי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says עם שבי is like ושבי, 'and the captivity of'.

4:10.headline: 'You did not return': said as if it already happened
4:10.body: ולא שבתם is in the past tense, but the prophet speaks of what is still to come. Metzudat David says the prophet knows they will not return, and the prophecy is so sure it is told as if done.

sources.quote: ואמר בלשון עבר כדרך הנבואה בהרבה מן המקומות כי הנבואה ברורה כאלו כבר נעשתה
sources.says: Metzudat David says he spoke in the past tense, as prophecy often does, because the prophecy is so clear it is as if it was already done.

4:11.headline: God 'overturned' you: by fire like Sodom, by exile, or removal?
4:11.body: Ibn Ezra reads הפכתי as fire sent from heaven, as at Sodom. Malbim reads it as the exiles that overturned the country, and the Targum renders it 'My word removed you far off'.

sources.quote: אש הורדתי עליכם מהשמים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says I brought fire down on you from heaven.

sources.quote: וכיון בזה על הגליות שהגלם מלך אשור מארצם
sources.says: Malbim says it points to the exiles, in which the king of Assyria took them from their land.

sources.quote: מקצת ארצכם בעודכם בה היא שממה כסדום ועמורה
sources.says: Radak says part of your land, while you are still in it, is desolate like Sodom and Gomorrah.

sources.quote: רָחֵיק מֵימְרִי יַתְכוֹן
sources.says: The Targum says My word has removed you far off, as the Lord removed Sodom.

4:12.headline: 'Prepare to meet your God': to repent, or to fight Him?
4:12.body: Rashi, Radak and the Targum read הכון as getting ready to return to God. Ibn Ezra and Metzudat David read it as mockery: get ready to fight Him, as if you could.

sources.quote: הִכּוֹן לִקְרַאת. לָשׁוּב מֵרִשְׁעָתְךָ
sources.says: Rashi says prepare to meet means to turn from your wickedness.

sources.quote: הכון לצאת לקראתו בתשובה ובמעשים טובים
sources.says: Radak says prepare to go out to meet Him with repentance and good deeds.

sources.quote: ועתה הכון והכון לך שתצא לקראת אלהיך להלחם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says now prepare yourself to go out toward your God to fight.

sources.quote: הכון עצמך אתה ישראל לקראת אלהיך להלחם בו
sources.says: Metzudat David says prepare yourself, Israel, to meet your God and fight Him.

4:13.headline: Whose שיח is it? The man's talk, his deeds, or God's plan?
4:13.body: שחו appears only here. Metzudat Zion reads it as speech, Rashi as a man's deeds laid out before him at death, and Ibn Ezra as what God means to do.

sources.quote: שחו. דבורו כמו או שיח לארץ
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says שחו is his speech, like 'speak to the earth' in Job.

sources.quote: כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו פּוֹרְטִין לְפָנָיו בִּשְׁעַת מִיתָתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says all his deeds are spelled out before him at the time of his death.

sources.quote: שחו, הוא הדבור הנפלט מן האדם בהשתקעות רעיונים מבלי דעת כונה
sources.says: Malbim says שחו is the speech that slips out of a person, lost in thought, without meaning to.

sources.quote: מה שיחו- מה רצונו לעשות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says מה שיחו is what He wants to do.

4:13.headline: יוצר, 'forming', gives shape; ברא makes from nothing
4:13.body: Maimonides says יצירה means giving a shape, which is why 'former of mountains' fits. He says ברא is bringing into being from nothing, and Malbim agrees: creation is something from nothing, forming is something from something.

sources.quote: כי נראה לי שיצירה מורה על מתן תבנית ומתאר
sources.says: Maimonides says it seems to him that forming points to giving a shape and an outline.

sources.quote: נותן להם תבנית
sources.says: Maimonides says that 'former of mountains' means He gives them their form.

sources.quote: כי זה לדעתנו הבאה לידי מציאות מהעדר
sources.says: Maimonides says that to us ברא means bringing into existence from nothing.

sources.quote: והיצירה הוא יש מיש
sources.says: Malbim says forming is something from something.

4:13.headline: 'Created רוח': a wind, or spirits placed in bodies?
4:13.body: Ibn Ezra and Radak read רוח as the wind: unseen and strong. Ibn Ezra also quotes Yefet, who reads it as spirits created in bodies.

sources.quote: ובורא רוח - שאיננו עומד על דרך אחד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the wind does not stay in one way.

sources.quote: וזכר רוח שהוא דבר חזק בנבראים ואינו נראה
sources.says: Radak says he mentioned the wind because it is strong among created things and cannot be seen.

sources.quote: ובורא רוחות בגויות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra quotes Yefet, who says He creates spirits in bodies.

4:13.headline: Dawn turned to darkness, or dawn for the righteous only?
4:13.body: Radak and Metzudat David read it as God turning the dawn into darkness whenever He wants. Rashi and the Targum read it as dawn light for the righteous and darkness for the wicked.

sources.quote: וכשירצה ישימנו חשך והוא קדרות השמש
sources.says: Radak says that when He wishes He turns it to darkness, the gloom of the sun.

sources.quote: לַצַּדִּיקִים כְּאוֹר נוֹגַהּ
sources.says: Rashi says He makes dawn for the righteous like shining light.

sources.quote: לְאִתְקְנָאָה נְהוֹר לְצַדִיקַיָא
sources.says: The Targum says He prepares light for the righteous.

4:13.headline: עיפה means darkness, perhaps from the eyelid closing
4:13.body: Metzudat Zion says עיפה means darkness, like 'a land of עיפתה' in Job. Malbim ties it to the word for eyelid: when the eye closes, it cannot see.

sources.quote: עיפה. ענין חושך כמו ארץ עיפתה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says עיפה means darkness, like 'a land of darkness' in Job.

sources.quote: עיפה מענין חשיכה, והומלץ מענין סגירת העפעף שאז לא יראה העין
sources.says: Malbim says עיפה is from darkness, and it was chosen from the closing of the eyelid, when the eye cannot see.

4:13.headline: 'High places of the earth': the proud, or the mountains?
4:13.body: Rashi reads במתי ארץ as the proud and arrogant, whom God brings low. Radak reads it as the actual mountains, which God treads on and topples by wind.

sources.quote: מַשְׁפִּיל גְּבוֹהִים וְגַסֵּי הָרוּחַ
sources.says: Rashi says He brings down the high and the proud.

sources.quote: וההרים הם במתי הארץ, והנה הוא דורך עליהם ומפילם
sources.says: Radak says the mountains are the high places of the earth, and He treads on them and throws them down.

5:2.headline: נטשה: left alone, or thrown down and smashed?
5:2.body: Metzudat Zion reads נטשה as abandoned. Rashi says anything thrown down and shattered in a field is called נטישה, and the Targum says she was dashed on the ground.

sources.quote: נטשה. ענין עזיבה כמו נטשתה עמך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נטשה means leaving, like 'You have left Your people'.

sources.quote: כָּל דָּבָר הַמּוּשְׁלָךְ וּמוּטָל וְנוּפַּץ עַל הַשָּׂדֶה קוֹרֵהוּ נְטִישָׁה
sources.says: Rashi says anything thrown, lying, and smashed on the field is called נטישה.

sources.quote: אִתְרְטִישַׁת עַל אַרְעָא
sources.says: The Targum says she was thrown down on the ground.

5:2.headline: 'Will not rise again': forever, or only for a long time?
5:2.body: Radak says לא תוסיף קום means a long time, not forever, and shows other verses where 'no more' did not last. The Targum limits it to 'this year', and Metzudat David says Israel returns in the future redemption.

sources.quote: לא תוסיף קום לזמן ארוך
sources.says: Radak says she will not rise again for a long time.

sources.quote: והנה מצאנו כמו לא תוסיף זה שאינו
sources.says: Radak says we find a 'no more' like this that does not mean forever.

sources.quote: לָא תוֹסִיף לְמֵיקָם שַׁתָּא הָדָא
sources.says: The Targum says she will not rise again this year.

sources.quote: אבל בגאולה העתידה ישובו גם המה כמו יהודה ובנימין
sources.says: Metzudat David says in the future redemption they will return too, like Judah and Benjamin.

5:5.headline: 'Do not cross to Beersheba': Rashi finds no idols there
5:5.body: Rashi notices the verse says 'do not cross', not 'do not seek', and concludes Beersheba had no idols: it was the last point from which a man could still turn back to Jerusalem. Metzudat David disagrees and says altars to idols stood there.

sources.quote: לֹא נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״אַל תָּבוֹאוּ״ וְ״אַל תִּדְרְשׁוּ״ אֶלָּא ״אַל תַּעֲבֹרוּ״, לָמַדְנוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה שָׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
sources.says: Rashi says it does not say 'do not come' or 'do not seek' but 'do not cross', so we learn there was no idol worship there.

sources.quote: לבאר שבע לא תעבורו כי גם שם בנו מזבחות לעכו״ם
sources.says: Metzudat David says do not cross to Beersheba, because they built altars to idols there too.

5:5.headline: Gilgal will 'go into exile': its name is its curse
5:5.body: The verse says הגלגל גלה יגלה: Gilgal will surely go into exile. Rashi says its name is its curse, and Metzudat David and Radak call it a play on words.

sources.quote: לְפִי שְׁמוֹ קִלְלָתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says its name is its curse.

sources.quote: והוא לשון הנופל על לשון
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is one word falling on another, a play on words.

sources.quote: דרך צחות, כמו עקרון תעקר
sources.says: Radak says it is a witty way of speaking, like 'Ekron shall be uprooted'.

5:5.headline: Bethel, 'house of God', turns into Beth-Aven: emptiness and trouble
5:5.body: Metzudat David and Radak say the prophet uses the insulting name Beth-Aven for Bethel. Rashi renders לאון as 'to vanity', Metzudat Zion as toil and trouble, and Radak plays it against אין, 'nothing'.

sources.quote: כי בית אל כינה הכתוב לגנאי בשם בית און
sources.says: Metzudat David says Scripture insultingly calls Bethel by the name Beth-Aven.

sources.quote: יְהוֹן לְלַמָּא, וְהוּא תַּרְגּוּם שֶׁל הֶבֶל
sources.says: Rashi gives the Aramaic 'they will be for nothing', which is the translation of הבל, vanity.

sources.quote: לאון. ענין עמל ויגיעה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says לאון means toil and trouble.

sources.quote: כמו שהיו קוראים אותו לגנאי בית און כי לאון ולאין תהיה
sources.says: Radak says it is as they used to call it insultingly Beth-Aven, since it will be 'to און and to nothing'.

5:6.headline: 'Lest it prosper like fire': a word for success used for burning
5:6.body: Rashi, with the Targum, reads יצלח as God's anger burning like fire. Ibn Ezra says it means to break through, as in 'they crossed the Jordan', and Malbim says a fire 'succeeds' when it finds wood to consume.

sources.quote: דִּילְמָא יִדְלַק בְּאֶשָּׁא רוּגְזֵיהּ
sources.says: Rashi gives the Aramaic: lest His anger burn like fire.

sources.quote: יצלח - יבקע, כמו: וצלחו את הירדן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says יצלח means will break through, like 'and they crossed the Jordan'.

sources.quote: הצלחת האש הוא אם מוצא עצים לכלותם
sources.says: Malbim says a fire succeeds when it finds wood to consume.

sources.quote: יצלח. ענין התגברות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says יצלח means growing strong.

5:6.headline: 'House of Joseph': God's fire burns it, or it burns itself
5:6.body: Rashi, the Targum and Metzudat David read it as God's anger burning the house of Joseph, meaning Ephraim's kingdom. Malbim reads the house of Joseph as the fire itself: Israel's civil war, in which neighbors devour each other.

sources.quote: פֶּן תַּעֲלֶה חֲמָתוֹ כָּאֵשׁ לְבֵית יוֹסֵף
sources.says: Rashi says lest His anger go up like fire against the house of Joseph.

sources.quote: דִלְמָא יִדְלַק כְּאֶשְׁתָּא רוּגְזֵיהּ בְּבֵית יוֹסֵף
sources.says: The Targum says lest His anger burn like fire in the house of Joseph.

sources.quote: בית יוסף. היא מלכות אפרים שהם מבני יוסף
sources.says: Metzudat David says the house of Joseph is the kingdom of Ephraim, who are from Joseph's sons.

sources.quote: שבית יוסף יצלח כאש. שעץ הבוער אוכל את שכנו הקרוב אליו
sources.says: Malbim says the house of Joseph itself will blaze like fire, as a burning log eats its nearest neighbor.

5:8.headline: Kimah and Kesil: one star group brings cold, the other heat
5:8.body: Metzudat David, Radak and Malbim say Kimah cools and Kesil warms, and the world needs both. Ibn Ezra describes Kimah as six visible stars.

sources.quote: כימה מקרר וכסיל מחמם
sources.says: Metzudat David says Kimah cools and Kesil warms.

sources.quote: כימה יש בה צנה גדולה ומקטרא לפירי
sources.says: Radak, quoting the sages, says Kimah has great cold and makes the fruit shrivel.

sources.quote: שכימה הם המזלות המביאים קור ומים
sources.says: Malbim says Kimah is the constellation that brings cold and water.

sources.quote: שכימה הוא זנב טלה וראש שור והם ששה כוכבים נראים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Kimah is the tail of the ram and head of the bull, six visible stars.

5:11.headline: משאת: a load he carried, or a heavy charge laid on him?
5:11.body: Metzudat David and Radak read משאת בר as the grain a poor man carried on his shoulder, which you take. Rashi says it is a burden: a loan on interest that you piled on him to take his land.

sources.quote: המשא של תבואה שעל שכמו
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the load of grain on his shoulder.

sources.quote: מה שיגע ונשא על כתפו מהתבואה לביתו
sources.says: Radak says it is what he toiled for and carried on his shoulder, from the grain to his house.

sources.quote: זְקִיפַת מִלְוֶה שֶׁהִפְקַעְתֶּם עֲלֵיהֶם הַשְּׁעָרִים
sources.says: Rashi says it is a loan on which you raised the prices against them.

sources.quote: וּמַשְׂאַת לְשׁוֹן מַשָּׂא שֶׁמַּכְבִּידִים עֲלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says משאת means a burden that they make heavy on them.

5:11.headline: 'Vineyards of חמד': lovely ones, or ones you coveted?
5:11.body: Rashi and Radak read כרמי חמד as precious, lovely vineyards. Radak adds a second reading: vineyards you coveted and took from the poor.

sources.quote: כַּרְמֵי חֶמְדָּה
sources.says: Rashi says כרמי חמד means vineyards of delight.

sources.quote: שהם נחמדים וטובים
sources.says: Radak says they are desirable and good.

sources.quote: שחמדתם אותם וגזלתם אותם מן העניים
sources.says: Radak gives another reading: vineyards you coveted and robbed from the poor.

5:12.headline: כפר: a bribe, or a ransom paid to escape a death sentence?
5:12.body: Metzudat Zion glosses כופר as ransom, and Malbim says it is always about capital cases, unlike a plain bribe. Radak reads it as money taken to save the guilty from a righteous opponent.

sources.quote: כופר. פדיון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says כופר means ransom.

sources.quote: כפר, הוא תמיד לפדות מדיני נפשות
sources.says: Malbim says כפר is always for redeeming from capital cases.

sources.quote: להציל הרשע מיד בעל דינו שהוא צדיק במשפטו
sources.says: Radak says it is to save the wicked man from his opponent in court, who is in the right.

5:16.headline: רחובות and חוצות: two kinds of street
5:16.body: Metzudat Zion says חוצות are market streets. Malbim says the רחוב is the wide open space in front of the houses, and the חוצות are the narrow back lanes where women and children stand.

sources.quote: חוצות. שווקים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חוצות are markets.

sources.quote: והרחוב הוא מקום הרחב שלפני הבתים ששם מתאספים העם והחוצות הם מקומות הצרים שאחורי הבתים
sources.says: Malbim says the רחוב is the wide place in front of the houses where the people gather, and the חוצות are the narrow places behind the houses.

5:17.headline: 'I will pass through you': not rescue, but Egypt's plague-passing
5:17.body: Radak links אעבר to 'I will pass through the land of Egypt', when God struck it. Malbim says Israel hoped His passing meant rescue, but it means ruin, and Ibn Ezra calls it a figure for His anger and decrees.

sources.quote: כי אעבור בקרבך להרע לך כמו ועברתי בארץ מצרים
sources.says: Radak says 'I will pass through you' means to do evil to you, like 'I will pass through the land of Egypt'.

sources.quote: שיעבור ה' בקרבם יהיה להם יום חשך ואפלה, כי יעבור בקרבם לכלותם ולהגלותם
sources.says: Malbim says the Lord's passing through them will be a day of darkness for them, because He passes through them to destroy and exile them.

sources.quote: טעם כי אעבר - דרך משל על חרונו ואפו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'I will pass through' is a figure for His fury and anger.

5:18.headline: Who 'longs' for the Day of the Lord? Mockers, or hopeful Israelites?
5:18.body: Rashi and Metzudat David say they are mockers, who said 'let Him hurry, let His work come'. Malbim says they honestly hoped for the Day of the Lord, expecting it to rescue them.

sources.quote: הָאוֹמְרִים ״יְמַהֵר יָחִישָׁה מַעֲשֵׂהוּ״
sources.says: Rashi says they are the ones who say 'let Him hurry, let Him speed His work'.

sources.quote: שהיו בני יהודה מלעיגים בדברי הנבואה ואמרו ימהר להביא יעודי הפורעניות
sources.says: Metzudat David says the people of Judah mocked the words of prophecy and said let Him hurry and bring the promised punishments.

sources.quote: והיו ישראל מתאוים ומצפים שיבא היום ההוא
sources.says: Malbim says Israel was longing and waiting for that day to come.

5:20.headline: אפל is darker than חשך: no moon or star at all
5:20.body: Malbim says חשך still has some נוגה, the light of moon and stars, but אפל has none. Radak says the day will have not even a little light.

sources.quote: שהאופל גרוע מן החשך
sources.says: Malbim says the gloom is worse than the darkness.

sources.quote: הנוגה אינו אור עצמי רק אור הירח והכוכבים
sources.says: Malbim says נוגה is not a light of its own, only the light of the moon and stars.

sources.quote: אפילו קצת אור אין בו
sources.says: Radak says there is not even a little light in it.

5:21.headline: 'I hate' versus 'I reject': two different things God says
5:21.body: Malbim says שנאתי is hating what was never loved, while מאסתי is rejecting what was first chosen. So some festivals He always hated, and others He once loved and now rejects.

sources.quote: והנה השנאה היא בדבר השנוא מעיקרא. והמאוס הוא בדבר שהיה נבחר תחלה ונמאס אחר כך
sources.says: Malbim says hating is of something hated from the start, and rejecting is of something first chosen and then rejected.

sources.quote: השנאה הוא הפך האהבה, והמיאוס הוא הפך הבחירה
sources.says: Malbim says hatred is the opposite of love, and rejection is the opposite of choosing.

5:21.headline: עצרת: a festival assembly, or being held back before God?
5:21.body: Rashi and Radak read עצרת as a festival gathering, with Rashi calling it your assembly's offering. Metzudat Zion and Metzudat David read it as being held or detained, like 'detained before the Lord'.

sources.quote: קוּרְבַּן כְּנִישָׁתְכוֹן, כְּשֶׁאַתֶּם קוֹרְאִים עֲצֶרֶת
sources.says: Rashi says it is the offering of your assembly, when you call an עצרת.

sources.quote: כי החג הוא עצרת כמו שאמר עצרת תהיה לכם
sources.says: Radak says the festival is an עצרת, as it says 'it shall be an assembly for you'.

sources.quote: ענין עכבה במקום כמו נעצר לפני ה׳
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means being held back in a place, like 'detained before the Lord'.

sources.quote: בעת שאתם נעצרים ומעוכבים לפני
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is at the time when you are held and detained before Me.

5:25.headline: Sacrifices in the desert? Not at all, or only by the Levites
5:25.body: The opening ה makes it a question. Rashi says Israel kept only one Passover in the desert, while the sages in Ibn Ezra and Radak say the tribe of Levi did bring offerings.

sources.quote: מַגִּיד שֶׁלֹּא עָשׂוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּדְבָּר אֶלָּא אוֹתוֹ פֶּסַח לְבַדּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it tells us that Israel did nothing in the desert except that one Passover alone.

sources.quote: והנה הטעם שלא הגישו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the plain sense is that they did not bring them.

sources.quote: וקדמונינו זכרונם לברכה אמרו: כי הלוים הקריבו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says our early sages said that the Levites brought offerings.

sources.quote: ומי היה מקריב שבטו של לוי שנאמר ישימו קטורה באפך
sources.says: Radak, quoting the sages, asks who brought them: the tribe of Levi, as it says 'they shall put incense before You'.

6:1.headline: At ease: no noise of an enemy reaches them
6:1.body: Malbim reads שאנן, at ease, as the opposite of שאון, noise: no enemy's shout troubles you. The next word, הבטחים, is different: they trust their own strength even while at war.

sources.quote: השאנן הוא הפך שאון, שלא ישמע קול נוגש ומטריד מבחוץ
sources.says: Malbim says the one at ease is the opposite of noise: he hears no oppressor troubling him from outside.

sources.quote: שהשאנן הוא מי שאין לו שום מלחמה ואין לו מחריד מבחוץ, והבוטח הוא הבוטח על גבורתו אף שיש לו מלחמה
sources.says: Malbim says the one at ease has no war at all, while the one who trusts relies on his strength even though he is at war.

6:3.headline: Pushing the bad day away, or moving toward it?
6:3.body: Radak reads המנדים as people who push the coming disaster far off in their minds. Rashi reads it the other way: by their deeds they move themselves toward that bad day.

sources.quote: המרחיקים יום הרע העתיד לבא עליהם
sources.says: Radak says they are those who put off the bad day that is coming to them.

sources.quote: אַתֶּם מְנִידִים עַצְמִיכֶם לְיוֹם רָע
sources.says: Rashi says you move yourselves toward the bad day.

6:3.headline: A seat of violence, or violence that ends them?
6:3.body: Radak and Ibn Ezra read שבת as sitting: judges who sit at the city gate and rule by force. Malbim reads it as stopping: they bring near the violence that will end them as a nation.

sources.quote: שתשבו בשער לשפוט חמס ועול
sources.says: Radak says it means you sit at the gate to judge with violence and wrong.

sources.quote: כי שבת, כמו מושב זקנים יושבי שער
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says שבת is like the seat of the elders who sit at the gate.

sources.quote: שבת מענין השבתה
sources.says: Malbim says שבת comes from the sense of making something stop.

sources.quote: חמס מלך אשור אשר ישבית אתכם מהיות גוי
sources.says: Malbim says it is the violence of the king of Assyria, who will stop you from being a nation.

6:4.headline: Sprawled on their couches, or making their beds stink?
6:4.body: Rashi first reads וסרחים as lying stretched out on their couches. He then brings the sages, who hear סרחון, a foul smell: they swapped wives and fouled their beds. Radak adds a third reading: long sheets hanging over the bed's edges.

sources.quote: מִשְׁתַּטְּחִין וּמַאֲרִיכִין עַצְמָם עַל עַרְסוֹתָם
sources.says: Rashi says they spread out and stretch themselves on their couches.

sources.quote: מַחֲלִיפִין נְשׁוֹתֵיהֶם זֶה לָזֶה וּמַסְרִיחִין עַרְסוֹתֵיהֶן
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages: they swapped wives with each other and made their couches stink.

sources.quote: מן וסרח העדף שנותנים על ערסותם בגדים ארוכים ורחבים
sources.says: Radak reads it from 'the part that hangs over', meaning long, wide cloths spread over their beds.

6:6.headline: Drinking from basins, or tossing cups to each other?
6:6.body: A מזרק is the large basin used in the Tabernacle. Radak says they drank wine from big basins, not cups. Rashi brings the sages, who hear the root זרק, to throw: they tossed their cups to one another.

sources.quote: אגן גדול כמו מזרק אחד כסף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a large basin, like the silver basin in Numbers 7.

sources.quote: במזרקים שהם גדולים שותים יין ולא בגביעים וכוסות שהם קטנים
sources.says: Radak says they drink wine from large basins, not from small goblets and cups.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיוּ זוֹרְקִין כּוֹסוֹתֵיהֶן זֶה לָזֶה
sources.says: Rashi cites sages in tractate Shabbat who say they threw their cups to each other.

6:7.headline: They wanted the best, so they go first into exile
6:7.body: The rich used ראשית, the finest oils, and were called ראשית הגוים, first of the nations. Ibn Ezra points out the turn: they reached for the first, so they will go first, בראש, at the head of the exiles.

sources.quote: הם בקשו ראשית הם יגלו בראש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they sought the first and best, so they will go into exile at the head.

sources.quote: כן בדברים רעים יאמר לשון ראש ומבחר על הרע שבכולן
sources.says: Metzudat David says 'head' can mean the worst of bad things, just as it means the best of good things.

6:8.headline: Does God say 'I desire' or 'I loathe' Jacob's pride?
6:8.body: מתאב looks like תאב, to long for. Rashi says it stands for מתעב, I loathe, and Radak says it means the reverse of longing. Metzudat David keeps the plain sense: God truly loves the Temple, yet will still hand it over.

sources.quote: מְתָאֵב. כְּמוֹ מְתָעֵב
sources.says: Rashi says מתאב is like מתעב, to loathe.

sources.quote: הפך תאבתי לישעתך
sources.says: Radak says it is the opposite of 'I long for Your salvation'.

sources.quote: באמת אני אוהב את גאון יעקב זה בה״מ
sources.says: Metzudat David says God truly loves the pride of Jacob, which is the Temple.

6:8.headline: God swears 'by His soul': what does that mean?
6:8.body: Radak says בנפשו here means 'by Himself', like 'by Myself I have sworn'. Malbim reads it as 'by His will', and Rashi as 'knowingly and on purpose'.

sources.quote: בעצמו כמו בי נשבעתי
sources.says: Radak says it means by Himself, like 'by Myself I have sworn'.

sources.quote: בנפשו, ברצונו. כמו ולא תגעל נפשי אתכם
sources.says: Malbim says בנפשו means by His will, as in 'My soul will not reject you'.

sources.quote: בְּנַפְשׁוֹ. מִדַּעַת וְכַוָּנָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means knowingly and with intent.

6:11.headline: The big house in splinters, the small one only cracked
6:11.body: Radak reads רסיסים like רצוץ, crushed, with ס in place of צ. Ibn Ezra says it means worse damage than cracks, and brings רסיסי לילה, the fine drops of night rain, as the other use of the word.

sources.quote: כמו קנה רצוץ ענין שבירה
sources.says: Radak says it is like 'a crushed reed', meaning breaking.

sources.quote: מדרך הענין שברים יותר מבקיעים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says from the context it means pieces broken worse than cracks.

sources.quote: ורבי משה הכהן אמר: כי רסיסי לילה גשם דק
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites Rabbi Moshe HaKohen that 'resisei laylah' is fine rain.

sources.quote: שֶׁיְּהֵא מְרוּסָּס לִבְקִיעוֹת דַּקּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the house will be smashed into fine cracks.

6:12.headline: Does one plow with oxen? Yes, but not on rock
6:12.body: The question 'does one plow with oxen?' seems to answer itself. Radak says the word 'rock' from the first half counts twice: do horses run on rock, and does anyone plow rock with oxen?

sources.quote: כי בסלע שזכר עומד במקום שנים
sources.says: Radak says the word 'rock' stands in place of two, serving both halves.

sources.quote: אָדָם בַּבְּקָרִים בַּסֶּלַע
sources.says: Rashi reads it as a man plowing on the rock with oxen.

7:1.headline: יוצר: forming a locust swarm, or gathering one?
7:1.body: Ibn Ezra reports a view that יוצר means joining or gathering, but he says the plain reading is right: God was making locusts. Radak gives both, gathering and forming.

sources.quote: כי יוצר כמו חבור, וכמוהו לפי דעתו יוצר עמל עלי חוק. והנכון: שהוא כמשמעו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Rabbi Moshe took יוצר to mean joining, but the correct reading is the plain one.

sources.quote: אסיפת הארבה כמו ויצר ה' אלהים מן האדמה כל חית השדה וגו' ויבא אל האדם לראות מה יקרא לו שענינו ויאסוף ויוצר שם בשקל ואת היותר החרמנו או פירש יצירת הארבה
sources.says: Radak says it may mean gathering the locusts, like ויצר in Genesis, or else forming the locusts.

7:1.headline: לקש: the late crop, or a word for locust?
7:1.body: Rashi, Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra read לקש as the late grass that comes up after the spring rain called מלקוש. But in his comment on Taanit 6a, Rashi says מלקוש can mean locust, with this verse as the parallel.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן מַלְקוֹשׁ שֶׁהַתְּבוּאָה עוֹלָה בְּקָנֶה שֶׁלָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says it is from מלקוש, the time the grain rises on its stalk.

sources.quote: כן יקרא העשב המאוחר כמו שנקרא מטר המאוחר בשם מלקוש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the late grass is called this, just as the late rain is called מלקוש.

sources.quote: ומלקוש לשון ארבה כמו והנה לקש אחר גזי המלך
sources.says: Rashi says מלקוש is a word for locust, like "and behold לקש after the king's mowing".

7:1.headline: The king's "mowings", or the shearing of his flock?
7:1.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read גזי as mowing: the king's first cutting of grass for his animals. Malbim reads it as shearing the king's sheep in midsummer.

sources.quote: אַחַר שֶׁגָּזְזוּ תְּבוּאַת הַמֶּלֶךְ עַד שֶׁלֹּא עָלְתָה בְּקָנֶה הָיוּ גּוֹזְזִין אוֹתָהּ שַׁחַת לְהַאֲכִיל לַבְּהֵמוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says they cut the king's crop before it rose on the stalk, as fodder for the animals.

sources.quote: מל׳ גזיזה וקצירה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from cutting and reaping.

sources.quote: אחר העת שגוזזים את צאן המלך שהוא באמצע הקיץ
sources.says: Malbim says it is after the time they shear the king's flock, in the middle of summer.

7:2.headline: "Who will raise Jacob up?" or "who can stand?"
7:2.body: Metzudat David reads מי יקום יעקב as "who will raise Jacob up". Ibn Ezra says the verb acts on no one: who can stand against this trouble. Rashi, quoting the Targum, reads it as "who will rise to plead for their sins".

sources.quote: כי מי יקום את יעקב לעמוד על עמדו לכלכלו ברעב
sources.says: Metzudat David says: who will raise Jacob to stand on his feet and feed him in famine?

sources.quote: ומלת יקום – מהפעלים העומדים בעצמם, ולא מן היוצאים על אחר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says יקום is a verb that stands on its own and does not act on another.

sources.quote: מַאן יְקוּם וְיִבְעֵי עַל חֲטָאֵיהוֹן
sources.says: Rashi gives the Aramaic: who will rise and plead for their sins?

7:2.headline: Jacob is "small": few, weak, low in rank, or wandering?
7:2.body: Radak says Jacob is small because a few are left of many. Metzudat David says he has no strength to feed himself, and Malbim says he is small in standing. Rashi quotes the Targum, which says מטלטלין, wandering.

sources.quote: ונשאר מעט מהרבה
sources.says: Radak says a little remains of what was much.

sources.quote: כי הוא קטן ואין בו כח ויכולת לכלכל את עצמו
sources.says: Metzudat David says he is small and has no strength or means to feed himself.

sources.quote: אחר שקטן הוא במדרגתו
sources.says: Malbim says he is small in his level.

sources.quote: כִּי קָטֹן. אֲרֵי מְטַלְטְלִין
sources.says: Rashi gives the Targum: because they are wandering.

7:3.headline: God "relented": changed his mind, or was appeased?
7:3.body: Metzudat Zion says נחם means turning a plan around, and Metzudat David says God regretted the decree. Rashi says God was satisfied by the prayer and answered, and Targum Jonathan says he turned back his anger.

sources.quote: נחם. ענין הפוך מחשבה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נחם means turning a thought around.

sources.quote: והנה נתחרט ה׳ על הגזירה הזאת ואמר שלא תהיה עוד
sources.says: Metzudat David says God regretted this decree and said it would not happen.

sources.quote: נִתְרַצָּה בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ וְנֶעְתַּר לִי
sources.says: Rashi says God was satisfied by his prayer and was answered to me.

sources.quote: אָתִיב יְיָ רוּגְזֵיהּ עַל דָא
sources.says: Targum Jonathan says the Lord turned back his anger over this.

7:4.headline: Judged "by fire": real fire, a burning drought, or sword and plague?
7:4.body: Ibn Ezra reads it plainly as judgment by fire, or else as fierce heat that dries up the rain. Radak's father said real fire, like Sodom, and Radak himself says the heat of the sun. Malbim says the sword and plague are pictured as a fire.

sources.quote: כמשמעו. לדין את העולם באש, כדרך כי באש ה' נשפט או שיחזק החום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is plain: to judge the world by fire, or else the heat grows strong.

sources.quote: פירש באש כמשמעו שרצה לדון אותם באש וגפרית כסדום ועמורה
sources.says: Radak says his father read it plainly: God wanted to judge them with fire and brimstone like Sodom and Gomorrah.

sources.quote: האש הזה אפשר שהיה דמיון לחום השמש החזק השורף המונע המטר ומיבש הצמחים
sources.says: Radak says the fire may be a picture of the strong heat of the sun, which holds back rain and dries the plants.

sources.quote: שהחרב והדבר נדמו כאש אוכלת במחנה
sources.says: Malbim says the sword and the plague were pictured as a fire eating through the camp.

7:4.headline: "The portion": the king's field, any field, or the land itself?
7:4.body: Radak says the word "the" points to the king's plot, as in "the king's mowings" in verse 1. Ibn Ezra says it names the kind, as in "ox and donkey". Malbim says it is the land held as an estate.

sources.quote: חלקת השדה אשר למלך כמו שאמר למעלה אחר גזי המלך
sources.says: Radak says it is the king's plot of field, as the verse said above, "after the king's mowings".

sources.quote: חלקת השדה וזהו שם המין, כמו: ויהי לי שור וחמור
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a plot of field and a name for the kind, like "I have ox and donkey".

sources.quote: החלק. הוא אחוזת הארץ
sources.says: Malbim says it is the holding of land.

7:5.headline: "Stop" instead of "forgive": the same plea, or a different one?
7:5.body: In verse 2 Amos said "forgive". Here he says "stop". Radak says the two mean the same, since if God forgives he will stop. Malbim says Amos could no longer ask for forgiveness, because a person is not forgiven a fourth time.

sources.quote: ולמעלה אמר סלח נא והענין אחד כי אם יסלח להם יחדל מלהרע להם
sources.says: Radak says above he said "forgive", and the idea is the same, for if he forgives them he will stop harming them.

sources.quote: ואומר חדל נא, עתה לא היה יכול לומר סלח נא, כי בפעם הרביעית אין מוחלים לו
sources.says: Malbim says now he could not say "forgive", because the fourth time there is no forgiveness.

7:7.headline: אנך is a foreign word for the lead weight on a builder's line
7:7.body: Rashi says אנך is Arabic for the lead weight on a line that a builder uses to straighten a wall. Ibn Ezra says the word has no match in Hebrew, and that in the language of Ishmael it is lead.

sources.quote: אֲנָךְ לְשׁוֹן עֲרָבִי חוּט קַו הַמִּשְׁקוֹלֶת הָעוֹפֶרֶת אֲשֶׁר בָּהּ יַבִּיט בּוֹנֵה הַחוֹמָה לְיַשֵּׁר הַדִּימוֹס
sources.says: Rashi says אנך is an Arabic word for the plumb line of lead by which the wall-builder looks to straighten the wall.

sources.quote: אין ריע לו ובלשון ישמעאל עופרת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it has no companion word, and in the language of Ishmael it is lead.

sources.quote: ואנך הוא בדיל בל׳ ערבי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says אנך is בדיל in the Arabic language.

7:8.headline: The plumb line God sets in Israel: strict law, or a personal measure?
7:8.body: Rashi and Radak say God will judge Israel by the line of strict justice. Malbim says Amos was not surprised by the wall but by the line still in God's hand after the building was done, a sign of judgment of each person.

sources.quote: הִנְנִי שׁוֹפֵט אוֹתָם בְּקַו שׁוּרַת הַדִּין
sources.says: Rashi says: I am judging them by the line of the row of judgment.

sources.quote: אשים בקרבם משקולת המשפטים
sources.says: Radak says: I will place the weight of judgments among them.

sources.quote: רק אני רואה ומתפלא על האנך אשר בידך שאתה אוחז אחר גמר הבנין
sources.says: Malbim says Amos wonders at the plumb line in God's hand, which he holds after the building is finished.

7:9.headline: "High places of Isaac" is spelled to sound like laughter
7:9.body: ישחק is the name Isaac, spelled with ש instead of צ. Metzudat Zion and Malbim say the spelling hints at שחוק, laughter and mockery, so the high places become a joke. Radak adds that Isaac was bound on the altar to do God's will, while his sons anger God at their high places.

sources.quote: כמו יצחק ויתכן שאמר ישחק לרמז שהבמות יהיו לשחוק וללעג
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is like יצחק, and he may have said ישחק to hint that the high places will become laughter and mockery.

sources.quote: וקראם ישחק מלשון שחוק ולעג
sources.says: Malbim says he called them ישחק from the word for laughter and mockery.

sources.quote: כתיב בשי"ן והוא כמו בצד"י כי שחק בשי"ן וצחק בצד"י ענין אחד
sources.says: Radak says it is written with ש but is like צ, since שחק and צחק mean the same.

sources.quote: לפי שיצחק אביו נעקד על גבי המזבח לעשות רצון האל יתברך ומצותיו והנה בניו מכעיסים האל יתברך בבמותיהם
sources.says: Radak says a possible reason for the name Isaac is that their father Isaac was bound on the altar to do God's will, while his sons anger God with their high places.

7:9.headline: "The sanctuaries of Israel": shrines, or strongholds?
7:9.body: Rashi says the sanctuaries are Bethel, quoting "for it is the king's מקדש". Metzudat David and Metzudat Zion read מקדש as a palace or stronghold. Malbim says they are the holy places at Bethel and Dan.

sources.quote: הוּא בֵּית אֵל שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי מִקְדַּשׁ מֶלֶךְ הוּא״
sources.says: Rashi says it is Bethel, as it is said "for it is the king's מקדש".

sources.quote: הארמונות החזקות של ישראל יהיו לחרבה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the strong palaces of Israel will become ruins.

sources.quote: ענין ארמון משגב וכן למטה מקדש מלך הוא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a lofty palace, as in "it is the king's מקדש" below.

sources.quote: שהם המקומות המקודשים אצלם בבית אל ובדן
sources.says: Malbim says they are the places they hold holy, at Bethel and Dan.

7:12.headline: "Eat bread there" is an insult: you prophesy for pay
7:12.body: Rashi says Amaziah means it with contempt: go where they will hand you scraps of bread for your prophecy. Ibn Ezra and Radak say the prophets of Israel, and the false prophets, prophesied for bread. Amos answers this in verse 14.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן בִּזָּיוֹן אָמַר לוֹ: שָׁם יִתְּנוּ לְךָ פְּתִיתֵי לֶחֶם בִּשְׂכַר שֶׁתִּתְנַבֵּא לָהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it is language of contempt: there they will give you crumbs of bread for your prophesying.

sources.quote: שהיו נביאי ישראל מתנבאים, בעבור פת לחם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the prophets of Israel prophesied for a piece of bread.

sources.quote: לפי שנביאי השקר היו מתנבאים לעם בפתותי לחם ובכוסות של יין או שכר
sources.says: Radak says the false prophets prophesied to the people for crumbs of bread and cups of wine or beer.

7:14.headline: "I am no prophet": I am not one for hire, or I was not one before
7:14.body: Rashi reads it as: I am not one of your false prophets who take pay. Ibn Ezra and Radak read it in the past: I was not a prophet before this. Malbim says prophecy was not his trade or his father's.

sources.quote: אֵינִי מִנְּבִיאֵי שֶׁקֶר שֶׁלָּכֶם הַנּוֹטְלִים שְׂכָרָם לְהִנָּבֵא
sources.says: Rashi says: I am not one of your false prophets who take their pay for prophesying.

sources.quote: לא הייתי נביא השם ולא בן נביא כי שומר בקר או חורש בבקר הייתי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra quotes Rabbi Moshe: I was not a prophet of God or a prophet's son, because I was a cattle keeper or plowman.

sources.quote: לא הייתי נביא מנעורי וגם לא בן נביא אנכי שלמדני דרכי הנבואות
sources.says: Radak says he was not a prophet from his youth, nor a prophet's son who taught him the ways of prophecy.

sources.quote: שאין זה אומנותי ולא אומנות אבותי
sources.says: Malbim says this was not his trade nor his fathers' trade.

7:14.headline: "Herdsman": a rich cattle owner, or a plain cattle keeper?
7:14.body: Rashi gives two senses: a herd-tender, and, following the Targum, an owner of herds, rich and not working for pay. Ibn Ezra says he was a cattle keeper or one who plows with cattle.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֲנִי עָשִׁיר וּבַעַל מִקְנֶה וּנְכָסִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁתִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: אֲרֵי מָרֵי גִיתֵי אֲנָא
sources.says: Rashi says Amos is rich with livestock and property, as Targum Jonathan renders it: I am an owner of herds.

sources.quote: בוֹקֵר אָנֹכִי. רוֹעֵה בָקָר
sources.says: Rashi says בוקר means a cattle shepherd.

sources.quote: כי שומר בקר או חורש בבקר הייתי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he was a cattle keeper or one who plowed with cattle.

sources.quote: כי בוקר אנכי ויש לי בקר רב ומקנה
sources.says: Malbim says he had many cattle and livestock.

7:14.headline: בולס: searching sycamores, mixing them, or a stammer?
7:14.body: Rashi says בולס is בולש, searching the sycamore trees, and says Amos stammered, so he said ס for ש. Metzudat Zion and Radak connect it with mixing, as in kneading. Ibn Ezra says the word has no companion in Hebrew.

sources.quote: וּבוֹלֵס כְּמוֹ וּבוֹלֵשׁ, אֶלָּא שֶׁעָמוֹס מְגַמְגֵּם בִּלְשׁוֹנוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says בולס is like בולש, except that Amos stammers in his speech.

sources.quote: ענין בלילה וערבוב ובדרז״ל שכן עני אוכל פתו מעיסה בלוסה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means mixing and blending, as in the sages' saying that a poor man eats his bread from a mixed dough.

sources.quote: או פירושו מערב השקמים עם דברים אחרים לצורך בקריו
sources.says: Radak says it may mean mixing sycamores with other things for his cattle.

sources.quote: ומלת בולס – אין לה חבר ובלשון ישמעאל כמו מיבש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says בולס has no companion word, and in the language of Ishmael it is like drying.

7:14.headline: Amos: named for being heavy in the tongue
7:14.body: Rashi quotes a saying that Amos was called עמוס because he was עמוס, burdened, in his tongue. He stammered, and Israel called him פסילוס.

sources.quote: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ עָמוֹס? שֶׁהָיָה עָמוּס בִּלְשׁוֹנוֹ, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹרְאִים אוֹתוֹ פְּסִילוֹס
sources.says: Rashi quotes: why was he called Amos? Because he was burdened in his tongue, and Israel call him פסילוס.

7:15.headline: "He took me" means he forced me
7:15.body: Ibn Ezra reads ויקחני as "I was compelled". Radak and Malbim agree: Amos did not leave his work by choice. God took him from his flock against his own will.

sources.quote: ויקחני - מוכרח הייתי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says: I was compelled.

sources.quote: לא הנחתי מלאכתי ברצוני כי האל יתברך לקחני מאחרי הצאן
sources.says: Radak says he did not leave his work by his own will, because God took him from behind the flock.

sources.quote: רק ה' לקחני ובחר בי נגד רצוני
sources.says: Malbim says God took him and chose him against his will.

7:16.headline: "Drip" means prophesy, or hint, or speak even a drop
7:16.body: Literally תטיף is to drip. Rashi says it is a word for prophecy and points to Ezekiel 21:2. Ibn Ezra says it is speaking in hints. Malbim says a drop is smaller than a prophecy, a short one, drop by drop.

sources.quote: וְלֹא תַטִּיף. לְשׁוֹן נְבוּאָה הוּא, וְהַרְבֵּה יֵשׁ בַּמִּקְרָא
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word for prophecy, and there are many in Scripture.

sources.quote: הוא מל׳ נטיפה והזלה ומושאל מענין הדבור
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is from dripping and flowing, and is borrowed for speech.

sources.quote: תטיף - כמו מדבר ברמז
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like speaking in a hint.

sources.quote: כי הטפה קטנה מנבואה, והיא נבואה קצרה כמטיף טיף טיף
sources.says: Malbim says a drop is smaller than a prophecy, a short prophecy, like dripping drop by drop.

8:2.headline: Summer fruit, קיץ, means the end, קץ, has come
8:2.body: Amos sees a basket of קיץ, late summer fruit. God answers with a word that sounds almost the same, הקץ, 'the end', and Maimonides says the thing was shown for the sake of its name.

sources.quote: כי קיץ ראית וקץ בא שהוא לשון הנופל על לשון
sources.says: Metzudat David says Amos saw קיץ and is told קץ has come: one word playing on another.

sources.quote: וכן ראִייתו של עמוס "כְּלוּב קָיִץ" (עמוס ח,א) כדי ללמוד ממנו על תום התקופה, ועל כן אמר: "בָּא הַקֵּץ"
sources.says: Maimonides says prophets sometimes see a thing for the sake of its name, and Amos saw summer fruit to learn that the end had come.

sources.quote: וקץ הקיץ אפשר שהם ענין אחד ושרש אחד
sources.says: Radak says קץ and קיץ may share one root and one meaning.

8:3.headline: 'Hush': a word Malbim reads as a hidden date
8:3.body: Plainly, the people carrying out the dead whisper 'hush'. Malbim notes the letters of הס add up to 65 and reads it as a hint that the northern kingdom would be exiled in 65 years.

sources.quote: ובחר במלה זאת שמספרו ס"ה, שבו רמז שבעוד ס"ה שנים כמנין הס יהיה הדבר הזה
sources.says: Malbim says הס has the number value 65, a hidden hint that the exile would come in 65 years, as Isaiah later says openly.

sources.quote: יאמר אחד לחבירו מן המשליכים הס כלומר נשתוק ולא נצעק
sources.says: Radak reads it plainly: those throwing out the dead say 'hush' to each other and do not cry out.

8:5.headline: Which month: the harvest month, or the extra leap month?
8:5.body: The grain sellers ask 'when will the month pass?' Metzudat David says the harvest month, when the poor eat gleanings; Rashi and the Targum say the extra month of a leap year, which pushes prices up.

sources.quote: יַעֲבֹר הַחֹדֶשׁ תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: מָתַי תִּתְעַבַּר הַשָּׁנָה וְיָבֹא חֹדֶשׁ הָעִבּוּר
sources.says: Rashi, following Targum Jonathan, reads it as the extra month of a leap year, which delays the new harvest so old grain gets dearer.

sources.quote: ר״ל החודש הידוע של הקציר כי בימי הקציר מוצאין העניים לאכול מהלקט והשכח׳ והפאה
sources.says: Metzudat David reads it as the harvest month, when the poor eat from the gleanings and need not buy grain.

8:5.headline: 'The Sabbath' here may mean the seventh year, or a week
8:5.body: השבת usually means the Sabbath day. Metzudat Zion and Rashi say here it is the seventh year, when fields lie fallow and grain is dear; Radak reads it as a week of putting the poor off.

sources.quote: והשבת. כן תקרא שנת השמטה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says השבת here is the seventh, fallow year.

sources.quote: מָתַי תָּבוֹא הַשְּׁמִטָּה וּּתְיַקֵּר הַתְּבוּאָה
sources.says: Rashi says they wait for the seventh year, when grain becomes expensive.

sources.quote: ודוחים אותם כן עד שתתייקר התבואה וימכרו לרצונם שבת שבוע
sources.says: Radak reads שבת as a week: they put the poor off from week to week until prices rise.

8:5.headline: Grain called שבר, 'breaking', because it breaks hunger
8:5.body: שבר usually means a break. Radak and Metzudat Zion say grain has this name because it breaks hunger, as in the Joseph story.

sources.quote: והתבואה נקראת שבר לפי ששוברת הרעב
sources.says: Radak says grain is called שבר because it breaks hunger.

sources.quote: שבר כן תקרא התבואה וכן נאמר שבר רעבון בתיכם (שם מ״ג) וזהו לפי ששוברת הרעב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the same, citing 'grain for the hunger of your houses' from the Joseph story.

8:7.headline: God swears by 'the pride of Jacob': Himself, or the Temple?
8:7.body: God usually swears by Himself. Radak and Ibn Ezra read 'the pride of Jacob' as God or His Name; Metzudat David, and Radak's second reading, take it as the Temple.

sources.quote: ר"ל כמו בי נשבעתי וכמו שאמר למעלה בנפשו והוא יתברך הוא גאון יעקב או ר"ל גאון יעקב בהמ"ק
sources.says: Radak gives two readings: God swears by Himself, the pride of Jacob, or by the Temple.

sources.quote: בגאון יעקב. בה״מ יקרא כן
sources.says: Metzudat David says the Temple is called the pride of Jacob.

sources.quote: הוא השם הנכבד שלא ידעו גוי, רק יעקב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is God's glorious Name, known to no nation but Jacob.

8:8.headline: Written 'watered', read 'sunk'
8:8.body: The written text has ונשקה, 'and it will be watered'; readers say ונשקעה, 'and it will sink'. Radak says both picture the land under water, like Egypt when the Nile floods.

sources.quote: ונשקה כתיב והכתיב ענין משקה כמו כי כלה משקה רוצה לומר שתהיה כלה מים והקרי ונשקעה הוא מבואר יותר שתהיה שקועה בתוך המים
sources.says: Radak says the written form means 'watered', all under water, while the read form means 'sunk in the water', which is clearer.

sources.quote: וְהוּא קָרוּי שִׁקּוּעַ שֶׁהַטִּיט הָעוֹכֵר אֶת מֵימָיו נִשְׁקָע
sources.says: Rashi says that when the Nile goes back down, the mud that clouds it sinks, and that is called sinking.

8:10.headline: 'A bitter day': the sages learn a mourning law from it
8:10.body: The verse compares the end to 'a bitter day', one day. The Talmud, as Rashi explains, learns from it that mourning by Torah law lasts only the day of the death.

sources.quote: דאנינות דאורייתא אינו אלא יום מיתה דכתיב (עמוס ח׳:י׳) ואחריתה כיום מר אלמא אין מרירות אלא יום אחד
sources.says: Rashi explains that Torah-law mourning lasts only the day of death, learned from 'its end like a bitter day': bitterness is one day.

sources.quote: דעיקר אבילות אינו אלא יום אחד דכתיב (עמוס ח) ואחריתה כיום מר
sources.says: Rashi says the core of mourning is one day, learned from this verse, and the seven days are a later rabbinic rule.

8:14.headline: 'The guilt of Samaria' is a name for an idol
8:14.body: אשמה means guilt. Metzudat Zion says an idol is called this after the guilt of those who serve it, and Radak says it is the golden calf at Bethel.

sources.quote: באשמת. מל׳ אשם וכן תקרא העכו״ם כן מאשמת עובדיה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says an idol is called אשמה, guilt, after the guilt of those who serve it.

sources.quote: ואשמת שמרון הוא העגל אשר בבית אל
sources.says: Radak says 'the guilt of Samaria' is the golden calf at Bethel.

9:1.headline: Wound them, cut them, or their wealth?
9:1.body: Rashi first reads ובצעם like ופצעם, wound them, and then as בצע, money: their wealth goes into exile first. Radak reads it as cutting them off.

sources.quote: וּבְצַעַם בְּרֹאשׁ כֻּלָּם. כְּמוֹ וּפְצָעֵם
sources.says: Rashi says ובצעם is like ופצעם, wound them.

sources.quote: וּבְצַעַם כְּמוֹ מְמוֹנָם יִגְלֶה בְּרֹאשׁ כֻּלָּם
sources.says: Rashi also reads it as their money, which will go into exile before everything else.

sources.quote: חמדת עשרם כמו בצע כסף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means their prized wealth, as in בצע כסף, gain of silver.

sources.quote: ופי' בצעם ענין חתיכה וכריתה
sources.says: Radak says the word means cutting and cutting off.

9:1.headline: Their 'end' means their children, or the common people
9:1.body: אחרית usually means the end or the last part. Metzudat Zion says here it means sons and daughters, and Radak says it means the ordinary people who come after their leaders.

sources.quote: ואחריתם. כן יקראו הבנים והבנות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says sons and daughters are called a person's אחרית.

sources.quote: וקרא העם אחרית לפי שהם אחרית לראשי העם
sources.says: Radak says the people are called אחרית because they come after the heads of the people.

9:3.headline: The snake on the sea floor: a sea monster, or strong nations
9:3.body: Metzudat Zion says this snake is the Leviathan, a sea creature shaped like a snake. Rashi cites the Aramaic translation, which reads it as nations as strong as snakes.

sources.quote: הוא הלויתן הדומה למראה נחש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the snake is the Leviathan, which looks like a snake.

sources.quote: והוא דג גדול דומה לנחש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a large fish that looks like a snake.

sources.quote: יוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: עַמְמַיָּא דְּתַקִּיפִין כְּחִוְיָא
sources.says: Rashi says the Aramaic translation reads it as nations that are strong like snakes.

9:6.headline: God's 'bundle' on earth: creatures, the righteous, or the elements
9:6.body: אגדה means a bundle of things tied together. Rashi says it is God's creatures, or the gathered righteous on whom the earth stands, while Radak says it is fire, wind and water bound in layers.

sources.quote: קְבוּצַת בְּרִיּוֹתָיו. דָּבָר אַחֵר: קְבוּצוֹת הַיְשָׁרִים הִיא הָיְתָה יְסוֹד הָאָרֶץ
sources.says: Rashi says it is the gathering of God's creatures, or else the gathering of the righteous, who are the foundation of the earth.

sources.quote: ואגדה הוא האש והרוח והמים שהם לאגדה אחת זה למעלה מזה
sources.says: Radak says the bundle is fire, wind and water, bound together one above the other.

sources.quote: ואגדתו - הם החיים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the bundle is the living things.

9:7.headline: Why compare Israel to the Cushites? Each commentator answers differently
9:7.body: Rashi says Israel has grown like the Cushites, who cannot change their skin. Malbim reads it kindly: Cushites stay recognizable wherever they live, and so will Israel in exile.

sources.quote: כַּכּוּשִׁיִּים אֲשֶׁר נִדְמֵיתֶם לָהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says Israel has come to resemble the Cushites, and cites 'can a Cushite change his skin'.

sources.quote: שהם מצויינים ונכרים תמיד ומיוחדים לאבותיהם
sources.says: Malbim says Cushites always stand out and are known as their fathers' children by their dark skin.

sources.quote: כבני כושיים שהם עבדים והם השחורים
sources.says: Radak says Cushites were sold as servants, and Israel, bought out of Egypt, should be God's servants.

sources.quote: הֲלָא כִּבְנִין רְחִימִין אַתּוּן
sources.says: The Aramaic translation reads it as 'like beloved sons'.

9:9.headline: What stays in the sieve: a pebble or a full grain?
9:9.body: Metzudat Zion says a צרור is a hard lump of earth. Malbim hears צרור, tied up: a full grain with flour bound inside it, like the faithful who do not fall through in exile.

sources.quote: צרור. חתיכה גסה של עפר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says צרור is a coarse lump of earth.

sources.quote: צרור, כן קורא גרעינים מלאים מקמח
sources.says: Malbim says צרור here means grains full of flour, the opposite of empty grains that fall through.

sources.quote: אבל הצדיקים הצרורים בצרור התורה והמצוה ואחדות ישראל לא יפלו ארץ
sources.says: Malbim says the righteous, bound up in the Torah and in Israel's unity, will not fall to the ground.

9:11.headline: David's kingdom is a sukkah because it shelters the people
9:11.body: Radak says the kingdom is called a סוכה, a booth, because it shelters (סוככת) the people. Malbim adds that a booth is a temporary hut, a picture of the weakened rule of David's line.

sources.quote: והיא הסוכה על דרך משל כי היא סוככת על העם
sources.says: Radak says the kingdom is the booth, as a figure, because it shelters over the people.

sources.quote: לא היה בית קבוע רק סוכת ארעי
sources.says: Malbim says David's line later had no fixed house, only a temporary booth.

sources.quote: יוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: מַלְכוּתָא דְבֵית דָּוִד
sources.says: Rashi says the Aramaic translation reads it as the kingdom of the house of David.

9:13.headline: Sweet juice named for the crushing that makes it
9:13.body: Radak says עסיס is any juice pressed from grapes or other fruit. He says it is named for the pressing, from the same root as ועסותם, 'you will tread down'.

sources.quote: ונקרא עסיס לפי שיוצא המשקה מהם על ידי סחיטה וכתישה מן ועסותם רשעים
sources.says: Radak says it is called עסיס because the juice comes out by squeezing and crushing, like ועסותם רשעים.

sources.quote: עָסִיס. יַיִן טוֹב וּמָתוֹק
sources.says: Rashi says עסיס is good, sweet wine.

9:13.headline: Hills that melt: soft ploughed soil, or flowing milk
9:13.body: Rashi says worked soil goes soft when the rains come, so the hills will be ploughed. Radak says it is a picture of hills melting under the milk that flows from the flocks.

sources.quote: תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: יִתְפַּלְּחָן, קַרְקַע עֲבוּדָה מִתְמוֹגֶגֶת בְּבֹא גְשָׁמִים
sources.says: Rashi cites the Aramaic 'they will be worked' and says farmed soil softens when rain comes.

sources.quote: כאלו הגבעות נמוגו ומתמוססת מרוב החלב שזב עליהן מן הצאן
sources.says: Radak says it is as if the hills melted from all the milk flowing on them from the flocks.

9:14.headline: Bring back the captives, or restore their old standing?
9:14.body: Metzudat Zion reads שבות as captivity, from שבי: God will bring the exiles home. Malbim reads it as their former rank: God will return them to the standing they once had.

sources.quote: שבות. מלשון שבי הגולה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says שבות comes from the captivity of exile.

sources.quote: וְאָתֵיב יַת גָלוּת עַמִי יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: The Aramaic translation reads it as 'I will return the exile of my people Israel'.

sources.quote: ושבתי את שבות עמי הוא השבת מעלתם ומדרגתם
sources.says: Malbim says it means restoring their high standing and rank.
